brief:
Danny Rahamim, describing himself as "probably the most left-wing person" on his kibbutz, struggles to reconcile his political beliefs with the aftermath of October 7, Al-Monitor reported. The kibbutz, located just a few hundred metres from Gaza, sits at the geographic and ideological centre of Israel's conflict with Palestinian territories.

The attack has tested longstanding progressive commitments on the kibbutz, a community historically rooted in socialist principles and left-wing activism. Members now confront tensions between their peace advocacy and security concerns brought into sharp focus by events of the past months.
dek: Danny Rahamim pauses for a few moments as he thinks about his neighbours here on an Israeli kibbutz just a few hundred metres from Gaza. "I'm probably the most left-wing person here," he said.
title: Israeli kibbutz leftists grapple with October 7 aftermath
